title: Installation & The Cargo Workflow
objectives: Install Rust with rustup and verify the toolchain
Explain what cargo build/check/run/test each do
Use clippy and rustfmt as part of every coding loop
body:
# Installation & The Cargo Workflow

## Installing Rust

`rustup` manages Rust versions:

```bash
rustup update
rustc --version
cargo --version
```

## The cargo commands you will live in

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo new x` | Scaffold a binary crate |
| `cargo check` | Type-check fast, without codegen |
| `cargo build` | Full compile to an executable |
| `cargo run` | Build then execute |
| `cargo test` | Compile and run tests |
| `cargo fmt` | Canonical formatting |
| `cargo clippy` | Lint for mistakes and non-idiom |

## Best practice: the `check` loop

Run `cargo check` constantly — it catches type/borrow errors in a fraction of
the time of a full build. Format continuously so diffs stay about meaning.
Treat clippy warnings as failing tests: fix them now.

## Reading compiler errors

Rust errors are teaching documents: error code, precise span, often a `help:`
suggestion. Read them top-to-bottom before changing code.

```text
error[E0382]: borrow of moved value: `name`
 --> src/main.rs:5:24
  |
4 | let greeting = format!("hi {name}");
  |                                ---- value moved here
```
